summary: The study compares two methods for depositing Al-doped ZnO films using ozone as the oxygen source. The first method uses sequential cycles of DEZ/O3 and TMA/O3 to control Al concentration, resulting in a layered microstructure. The second method involves coinjection of DEZ and TMA during each cycle, leading to a homogeneous distribution of Al. The films were characterized for their structural, electrical, and optical properties, with the coinjection method showing superior performance.
evidence: Aluminum-doped ZnO ﬁlms were prepared by atomic layer deposition at 250 /C14 C using diethylzinc (DEZ), trimethylaluminum (TMA), and ozone as the precursors. Two deposition methods were compared to assess their impact on the composition, structural, electrical, and optical properties as a function of Al concentration.
